description: Activity, accounts, issues and mail volume of a Redmine installation, as exposed by the redmine_expert_metrics plugin on /metrics. Pick your Prometheus datasource above - nothing else needs configuring.

panels.title: Active users (5 min)
panels.description:
Distinct users with at least one browser request in the last 5 min. Derived from Redmine's session tokens, so API-key requests and the mail fetcher do not count.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Active users (15 min)
panels.description:
Distinct users with at least one browser request in the last 15 min. Derived from Redmine's session tokens, so API-key requests and the mail fetcher do not count.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Active users (60 min)
panels.description:
Distinct users with at least one browser request in the last 60 min. Derived from Redmine's session tokens, so API-key requests and the mail fetcher do not count.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Logged-in sessions
panels.description:
Session tokens Redmine would still accept — active or idle.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Logins (24 h)
panels.description:
Distinct users whose last login is within the last 24 hours.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Instances scraped
panels.description: Redmine pods answering /metrics. Counted from redmine_info rather than from `up`, which would count every scrape target in the Prometheus. They all report identical numbers - this is the number of targets, not the load.

panels.title: Active users
panels.description:
Distinct users per activity window.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Logged-in sessions
panels.description:
Session tokens Redmine would still accept. Higher than the active-user count: a session stays valid while nobody is clicking.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: User accounts by status
panels.description:
Accounts by status — active, registered (awaiting activation) and locked.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Open issues
panels.description:
Issues whose status is not flagged as closed. Closed issues are kept out of this panel on purpose: they outnumber the open ones by orders of magnitude and would flatten the line to nothing.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Issues
panels.description:
Open and closed issues over the whole installation.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Active projects
panels.description:
Projects in status active (archived and closed ones are not counted).

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — with two pods, `sum` would double it.

panels.title: Helpdesk customer mail (per hour)
panels.description:
Mail recorded by redmine_expert_helpdesk: in = received from customers, out = sent to customers (replies, autoresponder, follow-ups), init = initial mail of a ticket opened in Redmine. Empty unless that plugin is installed.

Cumulative counter: the rate is taken per scrape target first and only then reduced with `max`, so a pod that starts mid-range cannot distort the result.

panels.title: Notification mail to Redmine users (per hour, top 10 projects)
panels.description:
Notification mails core delivered, one per recipient. An empty project label means an account or security mail, which belongs to no project.

Cumulative counter: the rate is taken per scrape target first and only then reduced with `max`, so a pod that starts mid-range cannot distort the result.

panels.title: Customer mail received (selected range, top 10)
panels.description: Mails from customers per project over the dashboard's time range. Rounded, because Prometheus extrapolates `increase()` on a slow counter and would otherwise report fractions of a mail.

panels.title: Customer mail sent (selected range, top 10)
panels.description: Mails to customers per project over the dashboard's time range — replies, autoresponder and follow-ups.

panels.title: Collection time
panels.description: Wall time of the last uncached collection. The snapshot is cached for 15 s, so most scrapes cost nothing; a rising line means the queries behind it are getting slower.

panels.title: Scrape up
panels.description:
1 while Prometheus can reach /metrics on that target, 0 when it cannot.

Joined against a 24h lookback on redmine_info for two reasons: `up` exists for every target in the Prometheus - sidecars share the Redmine job label - and a target that stops answering would otherwise go stale and vanish from the panel instead of dropping to 0. Within 24h of its last successful scrape, a dead target stays visible.

panels.title: Instances
panels.description: Redmine and plugin version per scrape target, straight from redmine_info.

panels.title: API users (today)
panels.description:
Empty unless *Record API usage* is switched on in the plugin settings.

Distinct users with at least one request authenticated by API credentials (key, HTTP Basic, OAuth) today. Who exactly is listed on the plugin's admin page (Administration » expert Metrics » API usage).

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum`.

panels.title: API users (7 days)
panels.description:
Distinct users with API requests in the last 7 calendar days, today included.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum`.

panels.title: API users (30 days)
panels.description:
Distinct users with API requests in the last 30 calendar days, today included.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum`.

panels.title: Users with an API key
panels.description:
Users holding an API key. A key carries the full permissions of its owner.

Every Redmine pod reports the same database-wide numbers, so this panel aggregates with `max`, never `sum`.

panels.title: API requests per hour by method
panels.description:
Requests authenticated by API credentials, by HTTP method. POST, PUT, PATCH and DELETE change data.

Cumulative counter: the rate is taken per scrape target first, deduplicated across pods with `max` per method and auth, and only then summed, so a pod that starts mid-range cannot distort the result.

panels.title: API requests per hour by authentication
panels.description:
key = X-Redmine-API-Key header or key parameter, basic = API key as HTTP Basic user name, password = login and password via HTTP Basic (scripts storing a password), oauth = OAuth token.

Cumulative counter: the rate is taken per scrape target first, deduplicated across pods with `max` per method and auth, and only then summed, so a pod that starts mid-range cannot distort the result.

panels.title: Issue page response time
panels.description:
Time Redmine spends on `issues#show` (HTML), from the request histogram: median, 95th and 99th percentile. Percentiles are estimated within histogram buckets (0.025 / 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 1 / 2.5 / 5 / 10 / 30 s), so read them as "which bucket", not to the millisecond.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum by (le) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", controller="issues", action="show", format="html"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", controller="issues", action="show", format="html"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", controller="issues", action="show", format="html"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Issue list and update (p95)
panels.description:
95th percentile of the issue list (`issues#index`, HTML) and of saving an issue (`issues#update`), the two pages next to the issue page that agents use most.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

targets.expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", controller="issues", action="index", format="html"}[$__rate_interval])))
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum by (le) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=~"$job", controller="issues", action="index", format="json"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Slowest actions (average, selected range)
panels.description:
Average time per request over the selected range, by controller and action. Actions that ran fewer than 5 times in the range are left out, so a single unlucky request does not top the list.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

targets.expr: topk(10, (sum by (controller, action) (increase(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_sum{job=~"$job"}[$__range])) / sum by (controller, action) (increase(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job"}[$__range]))) and on (controller, action) (sum by (controller, action) (increase(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job"}[$__range])) >= 5))

panels.title: Where the time goes
panels.description:
Seconds per second of wall time, all requests: time in SQL statements, in rendering views (without SQL) and in plugin hook listeners, next to the total. Hook time overlaps the other two — a hook that queries or renders counts there as well — so the lines are not stacked.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: SQL statements per request (top 10 actions)
panels.description:
Statements sent to the database per request, by action (query-cache hits not counted). A number that climbs over time on the same action usually means a query per row or per journal.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

targets.expr: topk(10, sum by (controller, action) (rate(redmine_http_request_sql_queries_total{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])) / sum by (controller, action) (rate(redmine_http_request_duration_seconds_count{job=~"$job"}[$__rate_interval])))

panels.title: Plugin hook time by listener (top 10)
panels.description:
Seconds per second spent in each hook listener class, summed over all hooks it implements. This is where a plugin that slows pages down shows up by name.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: Memory per pod (RSS)
panels.description:
Resident memory of each Redmine process. A line that only climbs until the pod restarts points at memory growth (fragmentation or a leak); compare with the container limit.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: GC time share per pod
panels.description:
Share of wall time each process spent in garbage collection (Ruby 3.1+). A few percent is normal; a share that grows with the process's age goes with growing memory.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: Puma backlog per pod
panels.description:
Requests waiting for a free Puma thread. Above 0 for longer than a moment means the threads are busy — slow requests or too few threads.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: Background jobs (p95 by job)
panels.description:
95th percentile run time of background jobs (ActiveJob) by job class, e.g. the helpdesk's AI summary or knowledge-base jobs. Jobs run inside the Redmine pods, so long ones take memory and threads from requests.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

panels.title: Server errors per hour
panels.description:
Requests answered with a 5xx status, by action. Requests killed before Redmine answered (pod restart, OOM kill) never reach Redmine's counters; those show up in the ingress or service mesh instead.

Per-process series: every pod reports its own share, so the query adds pods up with `sum` (unlike the rest of this dashboard). Only present while *Record performance metrics* is switched on.

options.content:
## Reading these numbers

**Every pod reports the same figures — except the performance row.** The plugin queries the Redmine database, so each replica answers `/metrics` with identical, installation-wide values. Every panel here therefore aggregates with `max`, never `sum` — `sum` would multiply everything by the number of pods. The *Performance* row is the opposite: request, hook, job and memory figures live in each process, so those panels add pods up with `sum` (or show them per pod). They appear only while *Record performance metrics* is switched on; slow requests themselves, with their slowest SQL and hooks, are on the plugin's admin page (Administration » expert Metrics » Slow requests).

**"Active" means a browser request.** It comes from Redmine's own session tokens, whose `updated_on` core bumps on every request (at most once a minute). API-key calls and the mail fetcher create no session token and do not count — this is "who would notice a restart", not "what load is the box under". API calls have their own row.

**Sessions outnumber active users.** A session token stays valid until it expires, so somebody who logged in this morning still counts as a session long after they stopped clicking.

**REST API.** Only while *Record API usage* is switched on in the plugin settings (off by default) — otherwise this row stays empty. Every request authenticated by API credentials is then counted in `redmine_api_requests_total` by `method` and `auth` (`key`, `basic` = API key as Basic user, `password` = login and password via HTTP Basic, `oauth`). `redmine_api_users` counts distinct users per calendar-day window. *Which* users and scripts is on the plugin's admin page (Administration » expert Metrics » API usage) — never in Prometheus.

**The mail metrics are counters.** Use `rate()` or `increase()`, as the panels above do. `redmine_helpdesk_mails_total` only exists when [redmine_expert_helpdesk](https://github.com/expertZentrale/redmine_expert_helpdesk) is installed; those panels stay empty otherwise. A notification with an empty `project` label is an account or security mail.

Metric reference: [redmine_expert_metrics README](https://github.com/expertZentrale/redmine_expert_metrics#readme).
